source.title: Enhancement: Shared branded PDF template designer — logos, contracts, invoices, letters, plans, schedules and bookings
source.body:
## Objective
Create one shared **Branded Documents & PDF Template Designer** module for all Sportarena / Gotmygame users. Coaches, referees, event organisers, physios, doctors, supply-chain sourcers/suppliers, sponsors and venue owners/managers can design their own contract, invoice and letter formats, upload logos and produce professional PDFs directly from their existing workflows. Extend to other authorised platform roles through a common capability rather than building separate designers.

Training/coaching plans, rehabilitation plans, event schedules, bookings and other operational outputs should carry the user's or organisation's approved brand. Branding must enhance presentation while preserving canonical business data, privacy and document integrity.

## Existing platform and backlog integration
Repository review in the preceding infrastructure assessment confirms Node.js/PostgreSQL, Expo React Native/react-native-web, the cap(...) REST/OpenAPI/MCP registry, durable jobs, encrypted sensitive data and existing local file routes. Indexed code search for PDF returned no matches; this is **not proof that no renderer/export already exists**. Before implementation inventory current invoice, contract, plan, schedule, booking, media and export code, screens and tests. Record existing behaviour → gap → smallest compatible enhancement.

Dependencies/boundaries:
- #247 owns scalable infrastructure, shared object storage, worker deployment and monitoring; consume those primitives while retaining local-development/legacy compatibility.
- #243 owns cross-module transactional email. This module supplies authorised PDF references/attachments to that service; it does not build a competing sender.
- #210 and #212 own physio/doctor practice, plans, billing and clinical controls.
- #145 owns sponsorship agreements; #231 owns legal matters/contracts.
- Canonical invoices/payments/quotes, bookings, appointments, teams/events, training/coaching plans, provider records and user/organisation identities remain authoritative. Rendering does not create a second finance, booking, clinical, contract or calendar system.
- Reinspect latest main before coding. A missing upstream structured plan/contract workflow must be tracked as a dependency; do not invent source data or silently implement an unrelated domain module here.

## 1. Roles and document catalogue
| Role/workspace | Initial template families and source integrations |
|---|---|
| Coach | Coaching agreement, quote/invoice/receipt, assessment summary, training/coaching plan, session schedule, progress letter |
| Referee/official | Appointment/engagement letter, assignment schedule, service quote/invoice, match report using permitted canonical results |
| Event organiser | Event programme/timetable, fixture schedule, booking confirmation, participation letter, supplier/sponsor agreement, invoice |
| Physio | Service agreement, invoice/receipt, authorised rehabilitation/exercise plan and progress summary |
| Doctor | Consultation summary, approved care plan, referral/clearance letter and service invoice; clinical authorisation/sign-off applies |
| Supply-chain sourcer/supplier | RFQ, quotation, sourcing/service agreement, purchase-order presentation, delivery note and invoice from supported canonical records |
| Sponsor | Sponsorship agreement, commitment/payment schedule, endorsement brief and authorised performance report |
| Venue owner/manager | Booking confirmation, hire agreement, invoice/receipt, facility timetable and event-use letter |
| Other authorised users | General business letter and supported personal/organisation document families |

A displayed template family must state whether its source workflow is available. Unsupported purchase orders, regulated certificates or legal-signature workflows must not be presented as completed integrations. Templates provide document structure; they do not guarantee legally valid agreements, tax compliance or medical authority.

## 2. Brand kits and uploaded assets
- Personal and organisation brand kits: primary/secondary logo, optional approved co-brand logos, colour palette, fonts, business/trading name, legal entity/contact/address, registration/tax identifiers where applicable, website, header/footer and optional stamp.
- Support multiple brands/branches per user where authorised; select the acting legal entity explicitly. Organisation membership alone cannot authorise changing its branding.
- Upload PNG/JPEG/WebP with transparent PNG supported; crop/fit, aspect-ratio lock, resolution warnings and reusable alignment/size presets. Validate actual bytes, size/dimensions, decompression limits and malware/quarantine policy; strip unnecessary metadata. Reject unsafe SVG/HTML by default unless a separately reviewed sanitisation pipeline exists.
- Private assets and scoped access by default; separate approved public brand assets from confidential signatures/stamps. Explicit permission to use sponsor/partner logos; no automatic brand endorsement.
- No broken/distorted logos, watermark covering body text or low-resolution silent stretching.
- Preserve an immutable asset/version reference in issued documents so changing a logo later does not rewrite history.
- Uploaded signature image is a visual mark, not proof of signer identity or a cryptographic signature. Restrict its use separately from ordinary logos.

## 3. Designer experience
Create **Documents & Templates** in common navigation and contextual actions in each source module: Preview document, Generate PDF, Download, Save to my documents and Share.

Responsive light-theme UI with:
1. Choose document family and starter template.
2. Choose personal/organisation brand kit and legal entity.
3. Edit layout/content with sample data.
4. Validate and preview using the actual PDF renderer.
5. Save draft, publish version and set permitted defaults.
6. Generate from a selected source record.

Use a practical block-based editor with drag/reorder and keyboard-accessible alternatives; a full unrestricted page-publishing tool is not required. Desktop/tablet supports page canvas plus properties; phone uses block/property editing and full-page preview without requiring precise dragging.

Supported blocks:
- Header/logo/business details, recipient/address, title/reference/date.
- Structured rich text, headings, bullets, terms/clauses and sign-off.
- Line-item and pricing/tax tables; totals and payment instructions.
- Training/coaching/rehab activity tables, goals/instructions and permitted exercise images.
- Event fixtures/timetables, sessions, venue/resource bookings.
- Page numbers, footer, confidentiality label, document status/watermark.
- Optional signature/acknowledgement placeholders and verification QR/reference where supported.

Controls: A4 and Letter, portrait/landscape, margins, spacing, alignment, sensible typography, repeating table headers, page/section breaks, header/footer on every page and keep-heading-with-content behaviour. A3 programme layouts are optional later. Warn on overflow, missing assets, unsupported fonts and low contrast. Display loading/empty/error/retry/conflict/permission states.

Offer polished starter designs: classic letterhead, modern invoice, professional agreement, weekly training plan, rehab/care summary, event timetable and booking confirmation. Provide a sample-data preview clearly labelled SAMPLE, not a fabricated real record.

## 4. Controlled data binding
- Versioned typed field catalogue per document family, with friendly labels and sample values. Examples: organisation.display_name, invoice.number, invoice.lines, invoice.tax_total, booking.start_at, plan.activities and event.fixtures.
- Allow only approved schema bindings and bounded conditional/repeating blocks. No arbitrary SQL, JavaScript, filesystem reads, remote fetches or executable HTML from templates.
- Server resolves source IDs, actor/entity, permissions, locale/timezone and permitted field projection. User-supplied field values cannot override invoice totals, confirmed booking dates, official results or clinical decisions.
- Required/optional/unknown distinctions; warn or block generation when required data is missing. Never silently turn missing values into zero, paid, signed, approved or medically cleared.
- Distinguish editable narrative/terms from read-only canonical values. Preview unresolved placeholders and validate before publication.
- All invoice arithmetic/currency/tax/discounts/credit adjustments and document numbers come from canonical finance services. The designer may choose placement/format, not recalculate authoritative money using client formulas.
- Templates cannot hide mandatory document fields/disclosures applicable to a configured family/entity. Maintain an explicit reviewed schema/policy, not a claim of universal jurisdiction compliance.
- Human-reviewed contract clauses and clinical text remain distinguishable from template/sample content. General templates cannot grant authority to issue prescriptions, medical certificates or legal advice.

## 5. Template ownership, sharing and lifecycle
- Scopes: private personal, organisation, and platform-curated starter. Sharing a template shares layout/approved assets, not patient/client/financial source data.
- Roles: owner, designer/editor, publisher/approver and document generator; implement smallest compatible permissions using existing organisation/delegation controls.
- Draft → published → retired with immutable published versions; duplicate/fork, rename, archive, restore and version history. Optimistic locking for concurrent editing.
- Defaults per user/organisation/document family/branch/locale with deterministic precedence; show which template/version will be used. No silent template changes after generation.
- Co-branded layouts require explicit authorised selection; a venue manager cannot use an unrelated sponsor's private kit.
- Team member departure/revocation removes future editing/generation access without deleting retained business documents. Define ownership transfer and orphaned-organisation handling.
- External sharing is document-specific, independent of template sharing. Public template marketplace is a later explicit feature; do not expose user templates by default.

## 6. PDF generation and source workflow behaviour
- Choose a maintained server-side renderer through an ADR comparing fidelity, table pagination, fonts/languages, security/isolation, licensing and resource cost. Prefer a constrained document schema compiled to controlled HTML/CSS or PDF primitives.
- Deterministic rendering from template version, brand-asset versions, approved source snapshot and render options. Embed supported fonts, selectable/searchable text, correct glyphs and locale-sensitive dates/amounts; preserve currency code and timezone clarity. Include Tamil and English test fixtures and evaluate RTL requirements explicitly.
- Use existing durable jobs for large/multi-page/bulk renders. Small renders may use a bounded synchronous path. Per-user/org quotas, job CPU/RAM/time/page/image limits, cancellation, retries/deduplication and cleanup prevent one user exhausting the platform.
- Preview and final PDF use the same engine. Contract/training-plan edits show accurate pagination before issue.
- Distinguish draft preview, generated export and formally issued/signed document. DRAFT/SAMPLE labels must remain visible where applicable.
- Store immutable issued PDF plus document metadata, template/asset versions, source references/snapshot, checksum, actor, generation/issue timestamps and relevant approval history. Protect sensitive snapshots with canonical encryption/retention controls.
- Regeneration creates a new version; changing template/source/logo does not alter an issued PDF. Existing issued invoices cannot be silently renumbered or edited; use canonical credit/replacement procedures.
- Define stale-source detection between preview and issue, and contract/clinical approval requirements. Patient-specific plan PDFs require live access plus publication/sign-off under the owning domain's rules.
- Generation does not confirm bookings, sign contracts, mark invoices paid, publish care plans or send emails. Each domain transition remains explicit.
- Batch output allows authorised selected records only, with individual status/errors, bounded size and expiring archive download. Never allow bulk rendering to bypass per-record permissions.

## 7. Secure storage, download and delivery
- Reuse canonical private-file storage and #247 S3 adapter. Every preview/download/regeneration/export rechecks permissions, organisation ownership and applicable patient/client consent/history scope. Deny insecure direct object reference access.
- Clinical/legal/staff/financial documents never become public due to a reusable template or branded logo. Apply data classification, region and retention policy to source snapshots, PDFs, temporary render files and backups.
- Run renderer with restricted filesystem/network, no arbitrary remote URLs, no internal metadata-service access, no template scripts and no untrusted executable content. Bound image decoding and PDF size.
- Short-lived authorised download URLs with clear expiry/revocation limits. For sensitive shared links requiring immediate revocation, enforce a gateway/access check rather than claiming an already-issued S3 URL can be revoked instantly.
- Share to named recipients/portal access using explicit scope/expiry; email delivery uses #243 preferences and secure links by default for sensitive content. Attachment mode requires appropriate document policy and limits; sending does not guarantee receipt or revoke downloaded copies.
- Audit template publication, brand changes, generation, issue, access/export/share/revocation; redact contents from logs, job payload visibility, analytics and notification previews.
- A QR/verification link exposes only deliberately approved authenticity metadata. Do not encode private medical data, bearer tokens or public-access secrets in QR codes.
- Digital signatures/e-sign provider integration are optional later adapters. Preserve legally significant signatures/bytes; do not confuse an uploaded signature image with validated signing.

## 8. Data/API contract and compatibility
Propose additive entities only where absent: brand kits/assets/versions, templates/versions, scoped permissions/defaults, generated documents/versions, render jobs and access/share records. Reuse existing jobs, file metadata, audits and canonical domain IDs.

Implement capabilities through existing cap(...) registry with Zod validation and REST/OpenAPI/MCP parity: manage brand kit, create/clone/edit/publish/retire template, list family fields, preview, generate, inspect job/status, list/download/share authorised documents. Binary transfer routes must enforce the same policy and be explicitly documented.

Use transactions, idempotency keys, uniqueness, deterministic pagination, indexes and optimistic locking. No unsanitised template evaluation, unrestricted model-generated HTML or client-provided private object paths. Existing templates/exports, invoice APIs, local development and legacy deployment must keep working behind compatible adapters/feature flags.

## 9. Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each listed role can select its authorised brand and generate at least one relevant document from existing canonical data; unavailable source workflows are explicitly identified.
- [ ] User can upload a logo, reuse it across invoice/contract/letter/plan/schedule/booking templates and preview accurate placement without distortion.
- [ ] Personal and organisation kit/template permissions prevent unrelated users or members without delegation from modifying or using private assets.
- [ ] Published template versions and issued document bytes remain unchanged after template/logo/source changes; replacements preserve history.
- [ ] Invoices preserve canonical identifiers, line items, currency, totals/tax and payment state; designer cannot forge financial values or remove required fields.
- [ ] Coach training plans and event schedules support multi-page tables, repeating headers and clear dates/timezones; physio/doctor outputs respect clinical approval and access scope.
- [ ] Cross-user/org, revoked-consent, youth/guardian, expired-share and direct object/download access scenarios are denied correctly.
- [ ] Preview-to-issue rejects or explicitly reconciles stale source/template versions; no race creates two issued financial document numbers.
- [ ] Renderer rejects executable templates, external/internal URL fetches and oversized/decompression payloads; resource/time limits and cleanup work.
- [ ] Duplicate/retried render jobs do not create duplicate issued documents or emails; worker failures recover with useful status.
- [ ] Visual QA covers A4/Letter, portrait/landscape, long names/addresses, many invoice lines, long clauses, absent optional fields, large logos, page breaks and Tamil/English fonts; no clipping/overlap/missing glyphs.
- [ ] PDFs have selectable text and sensible reading order; accessibility capabilities/limitations are documented without claiming PDF/UA certification unless tested.
- [ ] Phone/tablet/desktop editor and source-module journeys support keyboard/screen readers, clear errors and accessible previews.
- [ ] Secure delivery integrates with #243; no automatic email or contract/booking/clinical transition occurs from merely generating a PDF.
- [ ] Existing finance/booking/provider/source-module regressions, PostgreSQL permission/concurrency tests, API/MCP parity and Expo web build pass.

## Delivery phases
1. Inventory, document schema/renderer ADR, brand kits and curated starter templates.
2. Designer, preview, versioning and shared render/storage/job APIs.
3. Invoice/letter/booking/training/event integrations; role-specific contract/clinical/sourcing adapters as canonical sources permit.
4. Secure sharing/email integration, batch generation, visual/performance/security verification and operational runbooks.
5. Optional governed template import/export, e-sign adapters and curated sharing extensions.

## Definition of done
Deliver usable designer and contextual generation journeys, source-to-field/permission matrix, documented schemas/APIs, additive migrations and rollback, starter-template examples, realistic multipage PDF fixtures with rendered visual QA, meaningful security/concurrency/integration tests, renderer capacity/cost and retention/incident runbooks. Document supported languages and domain dependencies. Do not merge or deploy automatically.
